streetview.pano_ids_note: the three Google panoramas a sight-line test over the LiDAR finds most open to the building (2024-08, 31-33 m, on Eden Crescent off its south-west end: 64-66%, 28% of its roof clear of buildings and trees). 34 panoramas lie within 80 m; the others see 18% or less.

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins). The three panoramas (2024-08) show the street end, which faces north-east (bearing 44.5 deg), with no shadow cast on it by its piers, its top storey or its canopy, and sunlit patches on the street in front: the end is in open shade, so the sun was behind it, past bearing 314.5 deg, which in August is after about 14:30 NZST; 305 deg and 25 deg up is about 15:00, inferred, not read from the photographs. Without this block the sun is the Clock Tower's July morning, low in the north-east and full on this end (round 0: building region luma p50 239 drawn, 141 in the photographs, p90 245 against 244). A sunlit street below the horizon (ground, groundshade, as Old Government House's) and exposure 1.3 bring the shaded white cladding to p90 233 against 241-254 in the photographs; at 0.8 it was 170. The median is then 158 drawn against 139: the kit's glass draws at luma 15-40, where the photographs' glass, reflecting the sunlit buildings across the street, is 90-130.

refine.note: min_gain 0.2 (else 0.01) keeps every panorama at its Street View camera. The sky masks take this building's shaded white cladding for pale sky (mdk1's wide view: the top storey's face and the left pier), so mdk1's search ran to its bounds on three of five axes (dy +1.0, dz -3.0, pitch +2.0) and moved the end's south-east corner from 30-37 px off the photograph to 68-82 px off. v8ia's (13% sky round the silhouette) and MH15's (12%) are not applied either way: their searches (dx +1.9, dz +0.4 and +2.6) disagree with a fit to the street end's own openings by 1.5-4 m, pulled by the white neighbours the masks count as solid. That fit is in parts/common.js; min_sky stays 0.2, and the masks are as tools/sky_mask.py makes them (no branches_deg: there are no bare branches).
